companyDescription: Quantum computing · Novera QPU hardware + Cepheus-1 108-qubit systems — $100M Dept. of Commerce LOI, NSF-funded Pittsburgh Supercomputing testbed, riding a sector-wide rally on reports the U.S. government may take equity stakes in quantum computing firms
priceNote: Up 9.3% today as quantum computing stocks broadly rally (IONQ, RGTI, SEALSQ all up) on reports the U.S. government is considering equity stakes in quantum computing firms — a sector-wide policy narrative, not company-specific news. Still well off the $58.15 52-week high, above the $12.53 low.
summary: Rigetti's Q2 2026 report (Aug 6, 2026) showed real technical and commercial progress — revenue $5.1M (+183% YoY) on Novera QPU sales, a $100M Letter of Intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce, and an NSF-funded Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center testbed deal — but the GAAP loss widened to $52.6M and the stock fell -4.4% after hours on buyer-concentration concerns. Since then, a sector-wide rally on reports of possible U.S. government equity stakes in quantum computing has pulled RGTI back up sharply. The real catalyst ahead is whether the DoC LOI converts to a funded agreement, alongside Q3 2026 earnings (date not yet announced).

risks: Revenue is still tiny ($5.1M in Q2 2026) against a $52.6M GAAP quarterly loss — heavy cash burn, and the stock has fallen after 3 of its last 4 quarterly earnings reports
Heavy customer/buyer concentration in Novera QPU hardware sales — a handful of customers drive most of the revenue

Today's +9.3% move (and the broader quantum-sector rally) rests on unconfirmed reports the U.S. government 'is considering' equity stakes — a policy walk-back or non-event would likely deflate the sector-wide premium quickly
The $100M Dept. of Commerce relationship is still a Letter of Intent, not a funded contract — LOIs can stall, shrink, or fail to convert to definitive agreements

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% on Jul 29, 2026, with 3 of 12 officials dissenting toward a hike — the most hawkish split since 2016. Unprofitable, high-multiple names like RGTI are among the most rate-sensitive in the market; a hawkish surprise before CPI (Aug 12) could hit this name harder than most on this dashboard.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE still 3.3% YoY, above target. A hot CPI print could trigger a broad risk-off in unprofitable growth/speculative tech — exactly the bucket RGTI sits in given its $52.6M quarterly GAAP loss against $5.1M revenue.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Pre-revenue-scale quantum computing names carry the highest rate-sensitivity on this dashboard — duration risk on future cash flows is severe when current revenue is this small relative to the loss rate.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM-HIGH within this dashboard — the government-stake/DoC-LOI narrative is policy-driven and somewhat macro-independent, but RGTI's fundamentals (tiny revenue, large loss) make it unusually exposed to any broad risk-off from a hawkish Fed surprise.
